ref_extractions.title: Data Analytics in Bioinformatics

ref_extractions.title: Context Modulates Perceived Fairness in Altruistic Punishment: Neural Signatures from ERPs and EEG Oscillations
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper investigates third-party punishment and fairness using ERPs and time-frequency analysis, but it is a separate study conducted at North China University of Science and Technology. It does not use the Fribourg openneuro_ds004000 dataset.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Related topic (fairness/ERP) but different dataset from China-based research group.

ref_extractions.title: Impaired social cognition in schizophrenia during the Ultimatum Game: An EEG study
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This is the original publication from Horat et al. at University of Fribourg that collected the openneuro_ds004000 dataset. It explicitly compares schizophrenia patients and healthy controls during the Ultimatum Game using EEG/ERP analysis, focusing on the FRN component in the responder condition.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: tmin/tmax aligned to stimulus onset; FRN analysis at 320-360ms post-stimulus
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Labels derived from clinical diagnosis in participants.tsv; ERP analysis comparing FRN amplitudes between groups
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Primary dataset publication - 24 HC and 19 SCZ participants, ERP analysis of P2 and FRN components, source reconstruction showing dorsolateral/medial PFC differences in responder condition.

ref_extractions.title: Anticipatory deficits in psychosis during social cognition task analysed by task-based EEG dynamic functional connectivity
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper by Padée, Richiardi, Missonnier et al. explicitly states it uses the previously acquired dataset from Horat et al. (2018) available at openneuro.org/datasets/ds004000. It performs dynamic functional connectivity analysis comparing schizophrenia patients vs controls during the UG responder condition.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: 700ms sliding windows: 6 non-overlapping windows starting at -2100ms plus 1 overlapping window centered on stimulus onset
ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Uses same 24 HC and 19 SCZ dataset; connectivity analysis in alpha (8-13Hz) and beta (14-30Hz) bands; labels from participant clinical diagnosis
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Direct data reuse confirmation: 'The dataset, previously acquired (Horat et al., 2018) and opened with this correspondence... Data used in this paper are available under a CC0 license at https://openneuro.org/datasets/ds004000.'

ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This study investigates empathy deficits in psychotic disorders using a Textual Empathy Test (TET) with textual scenarios, not EEG recording. No Ultimatum Game paradigm or openneuro dataset is used.

feasibility_reason: The dataset has a well-defined event structure with clear stimulus and response markers, and two relevant references (10.1016/j.schres.2017.05.037 and 10.1016/j.schres.2023.01.029) directly support binary classification tasks (healthy controls vs schizophrenia patients) during Ultimatum Game responder condition with proper epoch parameters and label definitions in analysis.md.
tasks_section:
## Tasks

### Classical Task 1: Group Classification - Schizophrenia vs Healthy Controls during Ultimatum Game Responder Condition (ERP Analysis)
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 0.5 s, target_events = [`Stimulus/S 64`, `Stimulus/S 96`, `Stimulus/S128`, `Stimulus/S160`]
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: `super`
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | `Stimulus/S 64` | 0 | Healthy control (HC) participant |
  | `Stimulus/S 64` | 1 | Schizophrenia patient (SCZ) |
- **Super Meta Notes**: Labels derived from clinical diagnosis (participants.tsv) not raw event markers. Kernel must load participant diagnosis from participants.tsv and merge with epoch labels based on subject ID. Responder condition markers identified from Stimulus/S codes. Analysis targets P2 and FRN components (260-360ms post-stimulus).
- **Evidence**:
  - DOI: 10.1016/j.schres.2017.05.037 — EEG study investigates differences in ERPs (P2, FRN) between 16 schizophrenic patients and 19 healthy controls during Ultimatum Game responder condition, finding reduced FRN amplitude in patients (p=0.009).
- **Kernel Notes**: Extract epochs aligned to offer/condition markers; merge with participant group labels from participants.tsv; verify Stimulus/S code mapping to responder condition from events.tsv.

### Classical Task 2: Group Classification - Schizophrenia vs Healthy Controls during Ultimatum Game Responder Condition (Functional Connectivity)
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_segmentation_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: segment_length = 0.7 s, overlap = 0.0 s, tmin = -0.7 s, tmax = 0.0 s, target_events = [`Stimulus/S 64`, `Stimulus/S 96`, `Stimulus/S128`, `Stimulus/S160`]
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: `super`
- **Target Definition**:
  | Segment | y | Meaning |
  |---------|---|---------|
  | Any segment | 0 | Healthy control (HC) participant |
  | Any segment | 1 | Schizophrenia patient (SCZ) |
- **Super Meta Notes**: Labels derived from clinical diagnosis (participants.tsv) not raw event markers. Analysis focuses on -0.7s to 0s pre-stimulus window during responder condition. Kernel must compute functional connectivity (e.g., imaginary coherence) within alpha band (8-13 Hz) for each segment.
- **Evidence**:
  - DOI: 10.1016/j.schres.2023.01.029 — Uses openneuro_ds004000 dataset to analyze EEG dynamic functional connectivity comparing 24 healthy controls and 19 schizophrenia patients during Ultimatum Game responder condition, finding significant fronto-occipital alpha-band connectivity differences in pre-stimulus window.
- **Kernel Notes**: Segment continuous data using fixed-length windows aligned to stimulus onset events; compute connectivity metrics in alpha band (8-13 Hz); merge segment labels with participant group from participants.tsv.

### Potential Task 1: Fairness Processing - Offer Acceptance vs Rejection Classification
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 0.8 s, target_events = [`Stimulus/S 64`, `Stimulus/S 96`, `Stimulus/S128`, `Stimulus/S160`]
- **Label Route**: `Annotation`
- **Meta Level**: `raw`
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | `Stimulus/S 64` | ? | Offer displayed (requires behavioral merge) |
- **Potential Notes**: Ultimatum Game paradigm inherently involves binary decisions (accept/reject). Behavioral response markers (`Response/R 1`, `Response/R 3`) available for 1588 trials. Merge stimulus-locked epochs with response data to derive acceptance labels. Extended tmax captures decision period beyond stimulus onset.
- **Evidence**: DOI: 10.1016/j.schres.2017.05.037 — FRN component analysis suggests sensitivity to offer fairness; acceptance decisions reflected in neural markers.
- **Kernel Notes**: Extract epochs to stimulus onset; merge with response data by trial; derive y labels from response type (accept=0, reject=1). Verify trial alignment between stimulus events and response markers.

### Normal Task 1: Proposer vs Responder Role Classification
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 0.5 s, target_events = [`Stimulus/S 64`, `Stimulus/S 96`, `Stimulus/S128`, `Stimulus/S160`]
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: `super`
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | `Stimulus/S 64` | 0 | Responder condition epoch |
  | `Stimulus/S 96` | 1 | Proposer condition epoch |
- **Normal Notes**: Multi-block design includes both responder and proposer roles. Stimulus/S codes S64/S96/S128/S160 likely differentiate conditions (responder vs proposer). Role-dependent differences in neural processing (mentalizing demands vs outcome evaluation) expected.
- **Evidence**: Paradigm description indicates both roles; DOI references indicate responder condition focus but not exclusive to this role.
- **Kernel Notes**: Verify code-to-role mapping from events.tsv; extract epochs per code; classify based on event ID.

### Normal Task 2: Condition-Specific Processing - Human vs Computer Partner
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 0.5 s, target_events = [`Stimulus/S193`, `Stimulus/S194`, `Stimulus/S195`, `Stimulus/S196`, `Stimulus/S197`, `Stimulus/S198`, `Stimulus/S199`, `Stimulus/S200`, `Stimulus/S201`, `Stimulus/S225`, `Stimulus/S226`, `Stimulus/S227`, `Stimulus/S228`, `Stimulus/S229`, `Stimulus/S230`, `Stimulus/S231`, `Stimulus/S232`, `Stimulus/S233`]
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: `raw`
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | `Stimulus/S193`-`S201` | 0 | Human partner offer |
  | `Stimulus/S225`-`S233` | 1 | Computer partner offer |
- **Normal Notes**: Paradigm includes human vs computer partners. S193-S201 (counts 215-774) and S225-S233 (counts 400-422) represent condition-specific stimulus markers. Split-half counts suggest role differentiation within partner type. Suffix pattern (S193-S201, S225-S233) may encode 9 conditions each.
- **Evidence**: DOI: 10.1016/j.schres.2017.05.037 — Mentions human partner offers; paradigm description explicitly states both partner types.
- **Kernel Notes**: Extract epochs to condition-specific markers; verify partner type mapping from events.tsv; classify based on marker range.
